title: Learn 97% of Claude in Under 16 Minutes
key_points: Memory Import: Go to settings > capabilities > start import, paste Claude's provided prompt into ChatGPT, copy ChatGPT's output about what it knows about you, paste back into Claude, click 'add to memory' — completes in under 2 minutes

Claude has three model power levels: Haiku (cheapest/fastest, good for summarizing 50 meeting notes), Sonnet (best for everyday tasks like email drafts), Opus (best for complex tasks like finding patterns and metrics), plus an adaptive thinking option that auto-selects

Gmail Connector setup: sidebar > customize > connectors > Gmail > log in — enables searching inbox, summarizing emails, drafting replies; can share Claude account with assistant so they can self-serve answers from your inbox

Calendar Connector enables scheduling, finding free time, and analyzing time spent — example prompt: 'Add 1 hour time block sometime before Friday for me to review our next YouTube outline' and Claude explains why it picked that time
Advanced calendar use: give Claude your quarterly/yearly goals, then ask it to analyze calendar and email to see if time spent aligns with achieving those goals — turns Claude into a business coach
Additional connectors available: Slack, Notion, GitHub, Google Drive
Artifacts creates working interactive mini-apps within chat — example: 'Build me a spreadsheet with sample data' with editable columns for sales reps, status, product sold
Interactive visuals: Claude builds live clickable visuals; example given was visualizing the 'height framework' for short-form videos by pulling context from connected Slack

Projects: sidebar > projects > new project — creates folders preloaded with context (internal documents, PDFs, instructions, chat copy-pastes) in knowledge section; team members can collaborate with shared chats
Projects pro move: create system prompt in instruction box to get consistent results every time, functions like former custom GPTs
Voice mode: desktop uses waveform button at bottom of prompt bar, mobile uses mic button — transcribes entire conversation; speaker mentions talking 3x faster than typing

Chrome extension: install from Chrome Web Store as 'Claude for Chrome' — takes snapshots of sites, scrapes data, clicks buttons, works inside browser; example: analyzing patterns in spreadsheet numbers

Cowork: separate desktop app feature (top left), requires toggling on 'computer use' in settings — Claude controls computer to execute multi-step tasks; example: 'Pull last month's sales numbers from HubSpot, drop them in Google Sheet, build summary chart, post on team Slack before Monday 9am'
Schedule Task: within Cowork type /schedule to schedule recurring tasks — example: every morning Claude reads inbox, sends summary, identifies urgent items

Claude Dispatch: within Cowork > Dispatch > scan QR code with phone > installs app > connects to computer — enables remote commands to computer; example: requesting pitch deck be sent to someone for feedback while at dinner

Claude Code: AI software developer using plain English; speaker shut down company for 2 days to train everyone; available in Claude app or terminal; Anthropic has full setup guide; example: 60-year-old CEO Todd built CEO dashboard in 3 days with no technical background

Claude Channels: use iMessage, Telegram, or Discord to chat with Claude Code remotely while computer runs — requires creating bot, pairing with Claude Code in terminal, setting up API keys; example: Arturo messaged Claude Code to check email/calendar and check into flight while running late

Claude Skills: train Claude for repeatable tasks; access via sidebar > customize > skills > browse/install or create own; thousands shared on GitHub; example: 'Humanizer' skill targets 20 specific AI writing patterns and rewrites in more human tone

Claude Design: accessed at claude.ai/design — creates pitch decks, one-pagers, landing page mockups, full apps, motion graphics; can match brand guides/styles; described as newest release; recently partnered with Adobe
summary:
The video presents 16 Claude hacks from Dan Martell of Martel Ventures, who states he builds AI products daily and uses Claude heavily. He opens by comparing using Claude like Google search to driving a Ferrari at 10 km/hour.

The first hacks cover migration and model selection. Memory Import transfers ChatGPT preferences and history to Claude in under 2 minutes through settings > capabilities > start import, pasting a prompt into ChatGPT, then copying its output back to Claude. The model selector offers three tiers: Haiku for fast/cheap tasks like summarizing 50 meeting notes, Sonnet for everyday tasks like email drafts, and Opus for complex pattern-finding work, plus an adaptive option.

Connector hacks follow, covering Gmail (enabling inbox search, summaries, and draft replies through customize > connectors > Gmail), Google Calendar (scheduling, time analysis, and comparing time allocation against quarterly goals), plus mentions of Slack, Notion, GitHub, and Google Drive connectors. A specific tip involves sharing a Claude account with an assistant for self-serve inbox access.

The video then covers creation features: Artifacts for building interactive apps in chat (example: editable sales spreadsheets), interactive visuals that pull from connected services like Slack to create clickable learning tools, and Projects for organizing context with team collaboration and system prompts that function like former custom GPTs.

Automation features include Voice mode (3x faster than typing with full transcription), Chrome extension for browser automation and data scraping, Cowork for computer control requiring the desktop app and 'computer use' setting (example: pulling HubSpot data into Google Sheets and posting to Slack), Schedule Task using /schedule for recurring automations, and Dispatch for remote computer control via phone app.

Developer-focused hacks include Claude Code (plain English coding — example of non-technical CEO building dashboard in 3 days), Claude Channels for coding via iMessage/Telegram/Discord while computer runs (example: checking into flight remotely), Claude Skills for repeatable tasks with thousands on GitHub including a Humanizer targeting 20 AI writing patterns, and Claude Design at claude.ai/design for creating pitch decks, landing pages, and motion graphics with brand matching, noted as the newest release with recent Adobe partnership.
